stem: In a mouse lineage-tracing experiment, cells are labelled at the outgrowth stage of kidney development. Weeks later, label is found in the collecting ducts, calyces, renal pelvis and ureter. No label is seen in the glomeruli, proximal tubules or loops of Henle.
oneliner: Mouse lineage tracing: label in collecting ducts, calyces, renal pelvis and ureter, none in glomeruli, proximal tubules or loops of Henle → origin?
ask: From which embryonic structure do the labelled cells most likely descend?

whyNot.A: Forms the **nephrons** (glomerulus to distal tubule); those structures were **unlabelled**
whyNot.C: Forms the **fallopian tubes, uterus and upper vagina**, not urinary conduits
whyNot.D: Forms the **bladder and urethra**; the labelled structures lie **above the bladder**
whyNot.E: A transient, **non-functional** early kidney that regresses and gives no collecting ducts or ureter

why: The **ureteric bud** is an outgrowth of the **mesonephric duct**. It branches to form the **collecting ducts, calyces, renal pelvis and ureter**, while the **metanephric mesenchyme** forms the nephrons.

idea.rule: Ureteric bud makes the urine-draining pipes; metanephric mesenchyme makes the filtering nephrons.
also: The bud induces the mesenchyme, and the mesenchyme induces the bud to branch
Failure of the bud to form leads to unilateral renal agenesis
Wilms tumor arises from metanephric blastema
The mesonephric duct also forms the ductus deferens and epididymis in males

stem: A 5-year-old girl has had three febrile urinary infections in the past year. Imaging of the right kidney shows upper and lower segments, each drained by its own ureter; the two ureters join into one just above the bladder. The upper segment is small and dilated. The left kidney and ureter are normal.
oneliner: 5F + three febrile UTIs in a year + right kidney with two ureters joining above the bladder (Y-shaped) + small dilated upper segment → ?
ask: Which embryologic event most likely explains these findings?

options.A: Incomplete recanalization of the proximal ureter
options.B: Fusion of the lower poles of the metanephric masses
options.C: Early splitting of the ureteric bud
options.D: Failure of the ureteric bud to form

whyNot.A: Gives a **single ureter** narrowed near the renal pelvis (ureteropelvic obstruction), not **two ureters**
whyNot.B: Gives a **horseshoe kidney** across the midline; hers is a **separate right kidney with two ureters**
whyNot.D: Gives **absence of the kidney and ureter**; she has a **doubled right system**
whyNot.E: A bladder-to-**umbilicus** remnant that leaks urine at the navel; it does not double a ureter

answer: Early splitting of the ureteric bud
why: Early **splitting of the ureteric bud** gives a **duplex collecting system** with a bifid or double ureter and upper and lower kidney segments. The small segment is often obstructed, and the system is prone to **infection**.

idea.rule: Early splitting of the ureteric bud gives a duplex system; no bud at all gives renal agenesis.
also: A second, separate ureteric bud gives complete duplication with two ureteric openings in the bladder
In complete duplication the upper-pole ureter inserts lower and more medially (Weigert-Meyer rule) and tends to obstruct
In complete duplication the lower-pole ureter tends to reflux
An ectopic ureteral opening below the sphincter causes constant dribbling in girls
